head: Dustin Moskovitz gave $100M to Future Forward’s super PAC.
deck: Beyond Anthropic’s announcement, the filings show outside gifts from other donors in the network. Moskovitz, a funder behind Good Ventures, gave $130M across the outside groups on file in 2016–2024.
note: The amounts are gross of refunds and include gifts filed under his trust. A contribution does not direct a committee’s spending.
bridge: How did Future Forward’s receipts and spending compare with other committees’?
source: Source · Federal Election Commission contribution records

head: House Majority PAC led spending for or against sitting members at $213M. Among the 22 spending leaders, Future Forward led receipts on file.
deck: Receipts are compared among the 22 committees that spent the most for or against sitting members.
note: The spending uses money from all donors. The receipts cover the money documented here. The filings cannot trace a receipt to a specific expenditure.
bridge: Who did the committees spend for or against from their first network receipts onward?
source: Sources · FEC spending and receipts, with documented issuer receipts

head: 74% of these committees’ all-donor spending went against Republicans.
deck: The filings name members serving on Nov. 26, 2026. A member can appear on both sides if committees reported spending for and against them.
note: The filings identify the committee that spent the money. They cannot trace an expenditure to a donor or establish coordination with a candidate.
bridge: What do the filings show about the people these committees opposed?
source: Source · Federal Election Commission outside-spending filings

head: Outside committees spent against Seth Moulton and Thom Tillis in different elections.
deck: One set of committees received money from Public First Action. The earlier cases involve committees funded by people on today’s network roster.
note: The filings show where money went. They give no reason for the spending or link a gift to an expenditure.
source: Sources · FEC receipts and outside spending, lobbying filings and public statements
